Had an amazing experience with Mumbai Dream Tours! A special thanks to Hardhik, who made this journey truly memorable with his incredible knowledge, guidance, and hospitality throughout the tour.

The 3-hour trek was one of the most unique experiences in Mumbai, covering iconic places like the world’s largest open-air laundry at Dhobi Ghat, the fascinating Dabbawala system, and the vibrant life of Dharavi. Hardhik explained every detail with so much passion and insight, making the entire experience engaging and meaningful.

Today this is a ‘SUPER HAPPY ME’ after realising that we really must leave our phones and all the gadgets aside and live and enjoy the beautiful experiences, which cannot be captured by any camera of this world. It can only be felt.
In the end I am so grateful to Sandesh for taking me to such a beautiful place.

featured_reviews.review_text:
The holy land pilgrimage organized by JENSON WORLDWIDE TOURS from 24th May,2025 to 7th June 2025 , was an unforgettable and memorable experience  for everyone.
We were 53 people from different cities such as Aurangabad, Vasai ,Pune and  Mumbai .
I am expressing my views on behalf of this group.
The tour operator ensured that our travel was most comfortable and enjoyable. We never had to wait for long hours at the immigration or other check points. Thanks to the travel officials who handled these issues very professionally and efficiently.
It is important to mention that the guides at all times and locations gave us historical and biblical information. We have gathered a wealth of information from this pilgrimage regarding our faith. Our prayer is become more meaningful after this  pilgrimage. Thanks to these guides who shared their information .
No one has any complaint with regard to our stay in luxurious hotels. The room service as well as the food with lavish buffet will be remembered for many years to come.
Some hotels were strategically located with breathtaking view. Such as the hotel facing the sea of Gallilee.
Besides the Biblical site visits , Jenson Tours gave us sufficient time to do our shopping , to carry back happy memories of the holy land. On such occasions they told us what to buy and where to buy .This information was very useful.
On several locations we could celebrate the Eucharist which made our pilgrimage even more meaningful.
We can honestly say that it was worth the amount spent for this pilgrimage. We can confidently recommend those wishing to visit holy land to travel with Jenson Tours. They are trustworthy and genuine.

featured_reviews.review_text:
My parents took the middle eastern tour in 2017 and absolutely enjoyed everything. My dad kept insisting he's going to take my sister and myself there again.

A week before dad passed away unexpectedly, he brought up the trip again saying "I'm going to take both my girls, will have to get in touch with Jenson soon." So that same year in 2019, we made the trip - myself with my sister and mom.

I'm always reluctant to go on tours with other people and would rather travel alone than in a group on a bus. But this was a very pleasant and well organised trip. Everything from the hotel to the food was amazing and of great standard. Mass was arranged everyday for us in different churches. We had different guides in each city/country and they were all very friendly and extremely helpful. On our last night in Egypt, we opted out of the Nile cruise dinner, and the guide was so lovely and booked us an uber back to the hotel while the rest of the folks boarded the cruise.

Jenson remembered my dad and when we told him dad's favourite church was the Church of All Nations (Gethsemane) In Jerusalem, he arranged for the mass to be offered to my dad. We're very grateful for that. We have lovely memories from this trip.

featured_reviews.review_text:
JAYA HE GVK NEW MUSEUM
Art and Culture : GVK CSMIA T2 is home to India’s largest public art programme, titled ‘Jaya He’, in the form of a 3.2 km multi-storey Art Wall, illuminated by skylights, that has over 5000 pieces of artwork and artifacts from every region & corner of India.
Possibly India’s largest public artwork project to date, Jaya He Museum at the Mumbai International Airport, spans across Terminal 2 and is a landmark corporate initiative to safeguard an immense cultural resource.

One of the few Installations I liked during my visit here:
1. Recycled & Unconventional Map of Mumbai
2.  Hawa Mahal in Turban denoting Vaayu (An element of panchmahabhuta)
3. Frozen Fire denoting Agni
4. Moving Constant- (Tanjore Paintings- Folk  Art Form)
5. Nomadic Tribes (Gadiya Lohar)
6. Vahanas (mount/vehicle) of a Hindu God
7. Palitana Painting (09/09/1934)
Special thanks to Ms.Ashwini Varma @ashwini_varma for a guided tour of the museum.
You can also plan your visit, for no matter how many times you transit through the airport, Domestic or International, it been created in a way that you will be see a new detail in these exquisite “narrative trails” rich in ethnographic stories every time you are at the Airport.
CSMIA gives you an opportunity to take a guided tour of the museum in the departures section. Called as Jaya He Safari, these tours can be availed for free as you depart from Terminal 2.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Shivaji Park is not just a ground — it’s an emotion for every cricket lover. If you really want to watch future superstars of Indian cricket in the making, this is the place to be. On the red soil of this historic ground, you’ll see young kids practicing with full dedication, sweating it out under the sharp Mumbai sun, chasing their dreams with bat and ball in hand.
There’s something special about standing there and watching them play. The sound of leather hitting the bat, coaches shouting instructions, and parents cheering from the side — it all feels raw and real. Many legends, including Sachin Tendulkar, began their journey here, which makes the atmosphere even more inspiring.
The park is huge, so even if you're not into cricket, it’s a perfect place for a peaceful walk or to just sit and relax. In the evening, the cool breeze and open space make it ideal for clearing your mind after a long day.
And of course, no visit is complete without trying the famous vada pav near Shivaji Park. The street food around the area is amazing — simple, authentic, and full of Mumbai flavor. Grabbing a hot vada pav after watching an intense practice session just feels right.

featured_reviews.name: Vivek Jadhav
featured_reviews.review_text:
There’s something special about Shivaji Park that you just can’t explain — you have to experience it.

Evening walks here hit different. The open ground, the calming sea breeze, and the energy of people around you create a vibe that feels both peaceful and alive at the same time. 🌅

The street food stalls are a whole emotion — from classic Mumbai snacks to quick bites, everything tastes better when you’re walking around with your people. 😋

Love how the place has something for everyone — kids playing cricket, fitness lovers using the open gym, elders enjoying their walks, and youngsters just chilling and soaking in the atmosphere.

And the best part? The crowd. It’s not just a park, it’s a cultural heartbeat of Mumbai. You’ll see real, raw Mumbai here — diverse, energetic, and full of life. ❤️

featured_reviews.review_text: Place which is close to every mumbaikars heart! Wonderful place to go and roam around. Especially in diwali the celebration done here the fire show is amazing! Lots of food options available near the garden also 2, 3 parks 1 open gym is available. Classes of different sports activities are available at SPG (Shivaji Park Gymkhana) also plenty of Indian cricketers are trained from this Ground so this has a special emotion!

featured_reviews.name: Amit Gurav
featured_reviews.review_text: Shivaji Park, officially Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Park, is a public park situated in Dadar, Mumbai. It is the largest park in the island city. Similar but bigger in size to Azad Maidan and August Kranti Maidan (formerly Gowalia Tank Grounds), it is of historical and cultural value because of the political and social gatherings it has witnessed, both in pre- and post-independence Mumbai. The 113,000 square metres (28 acres) of open space is renowned as having been a cradle of the game of cricket in India.

featured_reviews.name: Ayaj Deshmukh
featured_reviews.review_text:
🌿 A Majestic Experience at Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Park
🏞️ Pride of Dadar, Mumbai | A Historic Ground of Courage & Culture 👑🇮🇳
Visiting Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Park in Dadar, Mumbai, was a truly memorable, emotional, and inspiring experience for me 💚. This park is not just an open ground—it is a historical landmark that carries the spirit of Maharashtra’s pride, unity, and rich legacy 🌟. The moment I stepped onto this vast green land, I felt a deep sense of respect and belonging 🙏.
The park is named after Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj, the great Maratha warrior king who symbolizes bravery, good governance, and Swarajya 👑⚔️. Standing here, I could feel the echoes of history in the air. This ground has witnessed many historic political movements, social gatherings, freedom-related events, and public speeches that shaped modern Maharashtra 🇮🇳📜. Knowing this made my visit even more meaningful and powerful.
As I walked through the park, I noticed people of all ages—children playing, elders walking peacefully, students practicing sports, and groups doing yoga 🏃‍♂️🧘‍♀️. The park beautifully balances history and daily life, showing how the past and present coexist harmoniously 🌸. The lush greenery and open space provide a refreshing escape from the busy city life of Mumbai 🌳🌬️.
One of the most emotional aspects of my visit was realizing that this very ground has been a platform for voices demanding justice, equality, and rights ✊. Many great leaders have addressed the nation from here, making it a silent witness to India’s democratic journey 🗣️📢. Being present at such a historically significant place filled me with pride and responsibility as a citizen 🤍.
The surrounding area reflects Mumbai’s cultural richness, with nearby temples, roads filled with local life, and a strong sense of Maharashtrian identity 🎭🪔. The park stands as a reminder that public spaces can unite people beyond caste, religion, and background, just like the ideals of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj himself 🤝.
As the evening breeze touched my face and the sky slowly changed colors 🌅, I felt calm yet energized. This place doesn’t just relax the body—it awakens the soul. It teaches us discipline, unity, and respect for our roots 🌱.
In conclusion, Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Park is more than a park—it is a living chapter of Indian history 🏞️📖. Every visit deepens respect for our heritage and inspires us to live with courage, integrity, and love for the nation 🚩✨.

featured_reviews.name: Raza
featured_reviews.review_text:
There’s something about Dadar Chowpatty that just feels like home. It’s not 'fancy' like some of the other beaches, but that’s exactly why I love it.
I came here last Tuesday after a really long day at work, and honestly, it was exactly what I needed. I just sat on the sand for an hour, watched the waves, and looked at the Sea Link glowing in the distance. It’s one of those rare places in Mumbai where you can actually hear your own thoughts.
I ended up chatting with an old uncle who’s been coming here for 30 years, and he told me the beach has its own rhythm. You see families laughing, couples holding hands, and students stressed about exams—all just co-existing.
A few 'human' tips if you go:
• The Chana Chor Garam: Get a cone from the guy near the entrance. It’s the perfect salty snack for a walk.
• The Rocks: Be careful if you sit on the tetrapods! They’re great for photos, but they can be slippery.
• The Timing: Go right when the sun is dipping. The sky turns this incredible shade of pink and orange that no camera can really catch.
If you’re feeling a bit overwhelmed by the city pace, come here. Buy a kulfi, kick off your shoes, and just exist for a bit. It’s good for the soul. ❤️
